claims.claim: This cohort experiences severe lag, stuttering, and frame rate drops during gameplay.

citations.review_text: This was one of my favorite childhood games,..so I bought it to show some love and relive those memories...but man this game made me suffer...I can ignore small performance issues yes but this game stutters like crazy and has constant FPS drops...Really frustrated and disappointed

This game is horrible I have a really good rig and it was laggy and i couldn't even get through the first mission spent all night trying to fix the lag checking my graphics and battery and everything else save your money and don't buy im so glad i got this game on sale if i paid full price for a broken game i would be even more upset about this.

Score: 1/5
Without the technical issues, I'd give it a strong 2/5.
If you like the GTA, Dead Rising, and/or Far Cry series, this is worth a shot.

When Steam is online, I got extreme lag/stuttering every 3-10 seconds, even in main menu and settings menu, at the lowest graphics settings on a modern machine. Simply put: Unplayable.

Offline, almost all technical issues disappear.

It is an over-the-top action-comedy romp.
Low difficulty. Simple mechanics and narrative.

Ultimately it was a boring, uninspired experience, with the gameplay, narrative/characters, and comedy not being enough to keep me invested for more than a few hours.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that progress fails to save properly, resetting players back to earlier penthouse missions upon reloading.

citations.review_text:
It doesn't save my game anymore...
Every time I "Save" and exit, when I go back in, I'm at the pent house mission again...

The game/story itself is great, although the mechanics are starting to show their age, but I'd highly recommend not getting this version, and I don't have the remastered version yet so I can't speak on if the remaster fixes the performance issues. The game runs rather smoothly at the start of the game, but it goes downhill in a really bad way as you progress through the story. The micro stutters and FPS issues constantly get worse, and for whatever reason there are some missions that after you complete them, the game permanently runs worse. The game also really doesn't like to do long play sessions. 

The game eventually ran horribly enough that I couldn't play anymore and moved to SR4, which has its own engine issues but not nearly as bad as this game. Specs don't seem to matter, obviously at this point everyone well exceeds the system requirements.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game suffers from frequent crashes on PC.

citations.review_text:
This game is a very satisfying sandbox with still to this day a really good character customizer. The way one of the six voices change your characters dialogue in the cutscenes is something I would actually like to see more of. 

The driving and unarmed combat are highlights for me, I haven't played a game that felt so good to drift with, you can pull Wheelies and stoppies on bikes and actually use the latter to turn sharply if you get the technique down. 

I would say saints row the third has the perfect mix of silly and serious, characters are allowed to have their serious moments, and for the most part a lot of the main plot is still played fairly straight. The stupidity lies in one of the two endings and especially the side minigames, which Imo is the best way to handle Saints Row. The later entries get too stupid and the gae reboot is obviosuly preachy self insert garbage. 

That being said, the game crashes ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ constantly on PC, its very dilligent about autosaves so you rarely lose very much, but it will happen like once every 1-5 hours and sometimes its a full system crash that takes over your PC until you restart. 

Eh, the remaster runs even worse, so I guess this is as good as it gets.
Glitchy pos, crash in middle of playing removes all progress I did. No auto save all all? Oh only sometimes...
See you back in Steelport.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that artificial intelligence characters frequently bug out during missions, such as failing to enter vehicles or running in circles.

citations.review_text:
fun braindead game. 
bugs here and there, very weird ai behaviour, etc (basically what you'd expect from this saga)
the start of the decline of the saints row ip imo. i just don't see the improvements over sr2. 
i liked it because coop is quite fun, you can spend a few hours with a dear one having some laughs. (kudos to my homie bfp)

overall 6 / 10, specially if you land like a huge discount ;) 

fyi: if you go for 100% achievement on the game:  
- play it coop from the start and do everything.
- save the game on different save files because you will need to do some missions twice choosing different endings (tower and ending mission to be precise)
- apparently there's an achievement about publishing something on their servers that can no longer be acquired via in game as far as i know because the servers are offline.

The plot is decent.
The gameplay is fine. It's sometimes unforgiving and overwhelming, but you can manage with upgrades.
The AI sometimes bugs out: slow-mo running, unable to enter the vehicle or just driving into stuff (it makes some Activities hell).
But the game is really fun. I prioritize gameplay over plot and this game has both. The plot is literally grasping for every reference to make itself as unserious as possible, and that's okay.
Sure, there are thing that I hate about this game, like Trafficking activities due to buggy AI, Survivals due to the amount of idle-ing you have to do or STAG's laser weapons either doing or not doing damage during missions (despite having fully upgraded character).
The third game was the point of moving into the world of pure fantasy, chaos and fiction. You thought it was the [b] 4rd [/b] game? Nah, this here is the real treasure.

Edit after 9 hours of playing: This is the worst experience Ive ever had played a game, it locks the least fun missions behind a mission the will block you from being able to complete it until you play 2 more hours of story that if you dont know to pick a certain option it will be over 4 hours more before you can beat it. It lets you unlock the cool cars by playing the game but if you think you can spawn those in to beat the repo missions 50% of the time nope you have to go across the map to try and move a helicopter from hundreds of enemies that will blow it up 9 times out of 10 before you can even take off. I will never touch a saints row game again after this Im glad to know the newest one got bad reviews because whoever approved this game should be fired and barred from ever touching a game again.

I love Saints Row and I do have fun playing this but it is the perfect example when I say I hate open world games, the ai will sometimes just not do the one thing it is supposed to like get in a car that has nothing blocking them instead they just run in circles getting shot by endless spawning enemies that just kill them as they stand still. Have had many times characters needed for missions just not spawn or vehicles get blown up immediately before you can get a chance to get near it to stop that. Online service got taken down so the game can never be 100% again

[h1] The Peak of Saints Row Chaos [/h1]  
Saints Row: The Third is easily the strongest game in the series. Its goofy, over-the-top, and still a blast even if it’s a bit dated now.

[h2] GOOD [/h2]  
[list]
[*][b]Still Fun Despite Its Age [/b]  
Yeah, it’s a little outdated at this point, but that doesn’t really stop it from being fun. The missions, humor, and general chaos still hold up, and it’s very easy to lose hours just messing around in Steelport.

[*][b]DLC That’s Actually Funny [/b]  
All of the DLC leans hard into the ridiculous tone, and most of it really lands. You’re not just getting filler add-ons, you’re getting more of the wild, stupid fun that makes the base game so memorable.

[*][b]Co-op Makes It Even Better [/b]  
Playing this with a friend takes everything up a notch. Co-op turns already insane missions into nonstop comedy, and the game is clearly built with that “mess around together” vibe in mind.

[*][b]Plenty of Features to Keep You Hooked [/b]  
There’s a ton of side activities, unlocks, customization options, and toys to play with. If this game grabs you, it can keep you busy for days.

[*][b]Gangstas in Space [/b]  
Gangstas from outer space… that alone tells you exactly what kind of energy this game is on. It fully commits to being absurd, and that’s a big part of why it works so well.
[/list]

[h2] BAD [/h2]  
[list]
[*][b]Crashes and Stability Issues [/b]  
It does have a habit of crashing now and then. The good news is that there are community fixes and guides out there that can help smooth things out, but out of the box, it’s not perfectly stable.
[/list]

[h2] Final Thought [/h2]  
At 9.99, the price isn’t bad at all, I will also highly recommend grabbing [url=https://store.steampowered.com/sub/17933/] Saints Row: The Third – The Full Package[/url] so you get every bit of content. It really is the strongest entry compared to the first two, and having all the DLC just completes the experience. If you’re going to jump into Saints Row,…

claims.claim: Reviewers find that certain long story missions crash and force players to restart entirely from the beginning.

citations.review_text: PLAY THIS GAME CO-OP. This is a beautiful open world game with non-beautiful story flaws. If you're playing to have fun and F around then it's perfect, but if you're playing for a concise and concluded story (which takes average 15 hours to reach the end) then this isn't the game for you. Every long main story mission like "Zombie Attack" or "Murderbrawl XIII" crashes and you have to restart all the way from the beginning just to get a unsatisfying end in the end of it all. The canon ending choice is letting Killbane escape to Mars while you try saving Shaundi, Viola and Mayor Burt Reynolds from a hostage/bomb situation by STAG officer Kia trying to frame you as a terrorist organization. You save your friends and defeat STAG, chase Killbane to Mars and finally it seems you kill him by stabbing him with a rock right in his ♥♥♥♥, but it turns out you're making A ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ MOVIE WITH HIM and you're all buddy buddy with him now and don't actually kill him?? The other ending (which also crashed when I tried to play through it) is letting Shaundi, Viola and Burt Reynolds die and killing Killbane by snapping his neck, but STAG make you seem like a terrorist and the whole city turns on you. Both endings leave you so unsatisfied with your choice that playing through the game genuinely means nothing at that point. I loved every minute of the gameplay, carplay, gunplay, upgrades whatever, but there are so much other games worth more of your time that this just isn't it.
Glitchy pos, crash in middle of playing removes all progress I did. No auto save all all? Oh only sometimes...

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the PC version of the game crashes frequently.

citations.review_text: IT CRASHES EVERYTIME AND ITS ANNOYING

This entry into the Saints Row series is far from perfect, especially coming from someone who has played absolutely everything, DLCs included. The character writing could use some work in places (they did my girl Shaundi real dirty, turned her into a generic 2012 "tough token girl" stereotype instead of the much more interesting characterization she got from SR2), and the PC version of the game crashes semi-frequently (I tend to get 1 crash per 8~12hrs of gameplay). However, it's a great deal of fun to do up the character customization, run the challenges and achievement hunt, and the combat is pretty smooth and fun.

claims.claim: Reviewers report visual issues with asset pop-in, such as grass rendering late and breaking immersion.

citations.review_text:
I'm not far into the game. i started by doing hit jobs and chop shop and buying properies. I just got the saints VTOL and it is the coolest vehicle i've ever seen in a game. to be fair there's lots of games i haven't played but yeah, that thing is cool as hell. my only gripe is that even at 1 star for cops or gangs they chase you relentlessly. and the pop in of like grass in such is so bad. i'd rather there was less of it then it popping up, breaks the immersion hard. and enemies are absolute bulet sponges. and i don't mean armored but like plain clothes enemies take a half dozen body shots. otherwise enjoying it so far

edit: just did the 3 dlc missions. they are all unnecessarily long, i just wanted them to end. and they don't delete off your mission list, i thought i was crazy. who'd want or need to redo them, and why wouldn't that be done like other missions area replayed?

edit 2: yeah, a lot of the missions are too long. like, i want to stop driving and killing and shooting down ships and move on to the next mission. and theres missions where theres an absurd amount of enemies and youre getting shot at from literally a dozen different spots. my brain just shuts off

After clocking over 420 hours in Saints Row: The Third, I can say this game delivers a wild, fun, and unforgettable open-world experience. The story is outrageous in all the right ways, the missions are varied and creative, and the over-the-top action keeps you coming back for more. The humor and style are absolutely on point, making it one of the best sandbox games I’ve ever played.

That said, the graphics feel a bit unbalanced. Some environments and character models look great and detailed, while others appear dated or lack polish, which sometimes pulls me out of the immersion. It’s not a dealbreaker by any means the gameplay and story more than make up for it but I think with a more consistent visual upgrade, this game could feel even more epic.

If you love chaotic fun, crazy customization, and a story that doesn’t take itself seriously, Saints Row: The Third is definitely worth your time. Just don’t expect it to compete with the latest AAA visuals.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that character customization offers good options, but is a step down from earlier entries in the series regarding clothing layers and freedom.

citations.review_text:
Saint Row The Third is a game that doesn't take itself seriously and only focuses on delivering a very entertaining experience. The story might not be anything to talk about but the game makes up for it in pure fun. 
The missions and characters feel like they came straight out of an cartoon, and the side content isn't tedious but rather fun to play. So fun that I've finished the game 100% twice and I'm willing to do it again.
The controls are very responsive and satisfying, and your character gets very overpowered in the late game if you grind money and respect which is very worth it. I could drive and fight gangs for hours without getting bored.
While I think the character customization is decent I'll admit it's a step down from earlier titles, not offering much freedom and feeling restrictive. But you can make nice outfits if you try.

If you're a fan of open world gameplay and funny storytelling that doesn't take itself seriously then I'd strongly suggest playing Saints Row The Third.

My introduction into the series and personal favorite Saints Row game. It's not the best one, Steelport is bland compared to Stilwater with little variety and few interiors, the story goes all in on being silly while often failing to actually be funny, and the customization takes a small hit since 2 in that you no longer have individual layers of clothing to control, but the gameplay is smooth, I like the characters, and the missions and side activities are a lot of fun. I'd put it among my top ten games from the 7th console generation. 8/10

'Saints Row: The Third' is pure chaotic fun in the city of Steelport & one of the reasons I love it is the music & overall vibe—it proudly leans into the silly, the wacky, & the completely unhinged in a way GTA would never dare. That opening bank heist mission had me thinking the entire game would stay at that level of hype… but wow, the pacing definitely zigzags. You get these tedious, grindy missions thrown in, the main antagonist gets taken out halfway through (like… what are we doing here?) & a core Saints member basically goes poof for most of the story. Still, even with the weird pacing & missed potential, I had a great time with it. With the right Co-Op partner, even the rough patches become part of the fun. It’s chaotic, messy, & over-the-top—but that’s exactly why I enjoy it!
